observations: Both CPU banks, two stored sentinels, two CPU addresses, three tile-byte pairs, two palette indices and both BG banks isolate transfer-end readback.
Every BG color is the same red marker, so data/bank/row/prefetch changes preserve visible LY/mode/frontier at every instruction clock within each timing group.
Normal-speed dot-264 reference reads match the high-plane byte of the background prefetch address in the CPU-selected VRAM bank, independent of the requested CPU address/sentinel.
Filling the otherwise unselected bank with 96 returns 96 in that bank; the earlier 00 is not a fixed cross-bank failure value.
SCY 0/3/7 row ramps select background rows 1/4/0. Substituting tile two at off-screen map column 20 returns D2/E3 from the CPU-selected bank.
All double-speed dot-264 reference reads remain FF; data controls do not qualify that as normal data access.
This is pinned SameBoy CGB-E software evidence, not independently validated hardware behavior. Production code, saved-state layout and private baselines remain unchanged.
